slot.brief: Give four small molecules/ions with their shapes and ask which one has a shape different from the rest (e.g. three bent, one linear or vice versa); pure VSEPR recall, no numbers.

stem: Which of the following species has a molecular shape different from the other three?

verdicts.working: CO2: 2 bond domains, 0 lone pairs → linear. I3−: 5 domains, 3 lone pairs (equatorial) → linear. XeF2: 5 domains, 3 lone pairs → linear. SO2: 3 domains, 1 lone pair → bent (~119°). Only SO2 differs.

working:
According to VSEPR theory, the molecular shape is determined by the number of bond pairs (bp) and lone pairs (lp) around the central atom:

1. $\text{CO}_2$:
Central $\text{C}$ atom has $4$ valence electrons and forms two double bonds with two $\text{O}$ atoms.
$$\text{Steric number} = 2\text{ bp} + 0\text{ lp} = 2$$
Shape: **Linear** (bond angle $= 180^\circ$).

2. $\text{I}_3^-$:
Central $\text{I}$ atom has $7 + 1 = 8$ valence electrons, forming two single bonds with terminal $\text{I}$ atoms and retaining $3$ lone pairs.
$$\text{Steric number} = 2\text{ bp} + 3\text{ lp} = 5$$
The $3$ lone pairs occupy equatorial positions of the trigonal bipyramid to minimize repulsion.
Shape: **Linear** (bond angle $= 180^\circ$).

3. $\text{XeF}_2$:
Central $\text{Xe}$ atom has $8$ valence electrons, forming two single bonds with two $\text{F}$ atoms and retaining $3$ lone pairs.
$$\text{Steric number} = 2\text{ bp} + 3\text{ lp} = 5$$
The $3$ lone pairs occupy equatorial positions.
Shape: **Linear** (bond angle $= 180^\circ$).

4. $\text{SO}_2$:
Central $\text{S}$ atom has $6$ valence electrons, forming two bonding domains with two $\text{O}$ atoms and retaining $1$ lone pair.
$$\text{Steric number} = 2\text{ bp} + 1\text{ lp} = 3$$
Shape: **Bent** (angular, bond angle $\approx 119^\circ$).

Thus, $\text{SO}_2$ is bent, whereas the other three species are linear.

Independent check: CO2: 2 bond domains, 0 lone pairs → linear. I3−: 5 domains, 3 lone pairs (equatorial) → linear. XeF2: 5 domains, 3 lone pairs → linear. SO2: 3 domains, 1 lone pair → bent (~119°). Only SO2 differs.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A: Mistakenly assumed to be the odd one out because it is the only species with zero lone pairs on the central atom, confusing shape with electron-pair geometry.
Option B: Mistakenly assumed to be bent by confusing the triiodide anion with $\text{I}_3^+$ (which has 2 bp + 2 lp and is bent).
Option D: Mistakenly assumed to be non-linear by forgetting that the three lone pairs in $sp^3d$ hybridisation occupy the equatorial plane, keeping the axial bonds linear.
